title: 2013 HMMT November Team Problem 6
statement: Points \(A, B, C\) lie on a circle \(\omega\) such that \(B C\) is a diameter. \(A B\) is extended past \(B\) to point \(B^{\prime}\) and \(A C\) is extended past \(C\) to point \(C^{\prime}\) such that line \(B^{\prime} C^{\prime}\) is parallel to \(B C\) and tangent to \(\omega\) at point \(D\). If \(B^{\prime} D=4\) and \(C^{\prime} D=6\), compute \(B C\).

solutions.text: \(\frac{24}{5}\) Let \(x=A B\) and \(y=A C\), and define \(t>0\) such that \(B B^{\prime}=t x\) and \(C C^{\prime}=t y\). Then \(10=B^{\prime} C^{\prime}=(1+t) \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}, 4^{2}=t(1+t) x^{2}\), and \(6^{2}=t(1+t) y^{2}\) (by power of a point), so \(52=4^{2}+6^{2}=t(1+t)\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)\) gives \(\frac{13}{25}=\frac{52}{10^{2}}=\frac{t(1+t)}{(1+t)^{2}}=\frac{t}{1+t} \Longrightarrow t=\frac{13}{12}\). Hence \(B C=\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}=\) \(\frac{10}{1+t}=\frac{10}{25 / 12}=\frac{24}{5}\).
